title: Prometheus Bound
subtitle: No pillars in the Caucasus here, but the basket is just as tightly bound.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What?!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: 23 Drachmae?! You're having me on!
Regulus's cry of surprise echoes far and wide, startling a few seagulls perched on the rooftop.
The young girl frowns viciously and lowers her voice.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Look, mate. I'm not asking for the bleeding moon here; I just wanna know where my APPLe is ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Or are you trying to pull one over on me? Even a whole bottle of fruit wine is only a sixth of a Drachma!
The bard rises to her feet, plucking the strings of her lyre with a smile.

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: My friend, what you're searching for isn't just any ordinary apple—it's a magical talking one.

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: Which means I will need to attend the celebration if I want to find it. After all, an apple as enchanting as Eris's banquet gift that brought Ilium to its ruin—could only be used as an offering to the gods.
The appeal to Greek mythology falls flat as it hits Regulus's ears. For whom only the stories of the gods of rock have ever held interest.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Yada-yada. Whatever you say, love. All I know is, what you're charging is daylight robbery!

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: You may be right.

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: But you won't find a better offer; not many people in my trade would trust an outsider who might just run off after I do my part.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: We won't ever do that! You can ask after Captain Regulus's reputation anywhere from the Thames to the high seas, and—
Familiar footsteps break up their tense negotiations.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Euphonia, remember that sneak you pointed out to me before? I need some extra hands to ...
They turn around and find a tall and strapping mercenary standing in front of them.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Oh, it seems you have another customer. I'll leave you to your work.

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: Not at all ... Welcome back, Eagle Bearer. I just didn't expect to see you so soon!

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: But did you say you need some extra hands? ... Let me think ... Eureka! I've got a plan ...
The bard murmurs to herself as a flash of inspiration crosses her mind.
She clears her throat and takes Regulus in one hand and Kassandra in the other with an amiable smile.

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: The fates have surely strung us all together for a reason!

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: You've come to ask about that weird magic apple—one quite likely to be used as an offering in the Dionysia.

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: And you, Kassandra, that strange man you asked me to investigate ... he claimed to be a craftsman repairing the Temple of Dionysos ...

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: I will hazard a guess that you've come because you need more hands to search out his co-conspirators.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Hang about, you don't mean ...

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: You are a clever one, miss! I do believe you will be able to assist one another.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Malaka, I knew it!
Fully aware of how cunning the bard is, Kassandra shakes her head. Time is running short—she must come to terms with the necessity of her situation.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: So, then we're all going to the Dionysia in order to look for someone.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: It shouldn't be too hard to look for a talking apple while I'm there.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Cheers, love! And we'd be happy to help with ... oh, erm ... Vertin, what's your take on this?
Regulus winks at the mercenary, who seems to appreciate the idea of some extra eyes on the festival.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Are you the one they call "Eagle Bearer"?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We've heard people singing of your exploits all over Athens.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They say the Eagle Bearer is a valiant hero, always willing to help those in need—a friend one can entrust their life to ...
The mercenary braces her hands against her sides and clears her throat.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: You two certainly aren't from around here; that's obvious.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: ... Huh?

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Everyone in this city knows; there's no amount of flattery that will affect my price.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Apologies, I've given you the wrong impression. I only meant to ask if the tales we've heard are true. I hope our cooperation can be built on mutual understanding.
Kassandra raises an eyebrow, surprised to be doubted by the very woman who had just praised her.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: It seems you've heard of my work already.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: I am Kassandra, the Eagle Bearer, and if you had any doubts, I will readily prove all that I am capable of.
She reaches out a hand to the girls.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: The name's Regulus, and this is Vertin.
She happily reaches out to grab Kassandra's hand.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Alright then, so how exactly are we going to help you?

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Simple.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: For now, all I need is more eyes around the city; do whatever pleases you, but keep a lookout for anyone suspicious.
A twinge of nerves creeps up Regulus's spine.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Athens is flooded with visitors in anticipation of the Dionysia; I won't be able to track every potential threat.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Right, well ... How do you know we aren't suspicious?
Kassandra examines the two figures; their modern clothing cutting a bizarre contrast to the world around them.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: I couldn't even begin to guess where you two are from.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: But that means you are most certainly not from Sparta, Korinth, or Phokis.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Which means you probably aren't here to kill Perikles.
Regulus takes a moment to digest this new information, before letting out a gasp.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: W-What! Kill Perikles?!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Wait-Wait a tick, are you asking us to keep our eyes peeled for ... bloodthirsty assassins!?

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: There's no need to be alarmed.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: I only need you to be my eyes. Just do as I say, and there will be no danger.
Regulus nods out of courtesy and whispers to the girl next to her.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Vertin, old pal, old chum, mate—I think we ought to reconsider this whole gig.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's just get this done, chum.
Her calm demeanor blunts Regulus's fears, but soon after her attention is captured by distant singing.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Huh, what's going on ...
The procession makes its way toward them, surrounded by a parade of people singing and carousing through the streets.

items.speaker: Drunken Passerby
items.text: Welcome to Athens—

items.speaker: Drunken Passerby
items.text: Have a toast, friends from afar!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Is this that party you mentioned?

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: The Dionysia, yes. You couldn't have picked a better time to blend in.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: And if you have time ... to have some fun.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We'll do our best to look for anything that might point to danger.
Regulus seems to have only heard half of Kassandra's words.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Have some fun ... But what about Mr. APPLe ...
She lowers her head, facing down a great dilemma.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Forget it, parties can wait! I'll do whatever I can to find you, Mr. APPLe!
Her voice fades into the growing festivities.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Vertin, you've got to vouch for me on this!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Dionysia, here I come!!!!

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Follow her, Vertin, and stay vigilant.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: I have my own work to do.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Understood.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Vertin, look at this pottery! Wouldn't something like this be a killer-diller in your lobby?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oh, and what do you think about this linen piece on me? I guess it's only suited for summer sailing.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ahem, Regulus, what happened to all that conviction from before?
The festival is full of attractions and distractions for the rocker pirate.

items.speaker: Festival Merchant
items.text: Hello ladies, how would you like to paint your very own festival mask?
They follow the sound of the barker's voice and discover an assortment of materials spread across the table—wood, leather, willow branches, rattan, minerals, and insect dyes in a variety of colors.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sorry, but we're a tad busy at the moment—

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: This is fab!
The festivities once again ensnare Regulus's attention.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: How about it, Vertin? Come on! Think of the attention! We'll be as famous as I was back when I was hosting APPLe Radio!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: My fans were bonkers! They'd crawl over glass for a signature! We sure could use some of them right now.

items.speaker: Festival Merchant
items.text: Haha, please come and try.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Just you wait, mate. This rockin' pirate is about to make a one-of-a-kind superstar mask in no time!
Regulus leans back to appreciate her "masterpiece," unaware that their new mercenary friend has returned.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Nothing unusual around the Dipylon Gate and the Temple of Erechtheion. What about—
Kassandra is speechless upon seeing their two peculiar masks.
Despite having crossed the Aegean far and wide and meeting many innovative poets, dramatists, and sculptors, she'd never seen anything quite like them.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: It's not exactly what I'd call an effective disguise.
She removes her mask and helps Regulus with hers.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I believe this may be a bit too fashion-forward for this era.
Kassandra seems about to question her choice of words, but is interrupted by another round of cheering from the crowded street.
The cheers grow louder as the crowd sings and sprays fruit wine into the sky.
Maidens in elegant dress balance fruit baskets filled with offerings on their heads; while the procession waves blazing torches in the air.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: No need to be startled. The Dionysia parade is just getting started.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: By the time they reach the agora, it will be even more lively.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: But that means the streets will be packed with people—a perfect opportunity for anyone with ill intent.
She deftly moves through the pulse of the crowd and waves her hand to the ladies behind.
After a clear eagle cry, Kassandra is nowhere to be seen.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: You watch the streets and I'll cover the high places.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: This is certainly a party ...

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Regulus, Vertin!

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Is that the strange apple you've been looking for?

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: I think I've found him.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Unfortunately, it seems he is about to fulfill his duty to Dionysos, as one of the sacred offerings.
